scope: Qualified OMP 18.0.9 macOS arm64, Windows x64, and Linux x64 clients; the digest-pinned RTX 5090 runtime image 12ef2d9e (runtime v0.5.1, source d956e6d6, binary 71edc2f6) under deployment profile qwen38-5090-v0.5.1 (the v0.4.8 context-cache arguments, configuration efacac23); the RTX 4090 durable v0.2.3 package (prefill chunk 2,048); the RTX 3090 durable v0.2.5-beta.1 package (131,072-token context). interpretation: All three GPU lanes are qualified in one public release; every claim binds an exact package, profile, and receipt.

Each lane runs its own best measured configuration rather than one shared configuration: the RTX 5090 context cache is sized so sibling forks of a stored template keep the shared base anchor (4/4 at 57.9K and 67.7K), the RTX 4090 prefill chunk moves to 2,048 (102,060-token session 68.0 s vs 84.9 s), and the RTX 3090 serves 131,072 tokens with exact retrieval at 130,048.

After a process restart a restored RTX 5090 session arrives warm: every sibling fork of the restored template is served on private_long_anchor whether an endpoint resume or a fork arrives first, and a 5 GB checkpoint restores in about 4 s instead of 24 s; a flipped payload byte is refused and quarantined.

The composed external-installation acceptance reran the docker-local runtime-side steps from the published v0.5.1 image through the lifecycle tool and carries the native public-URL install acceptances by hash because those components are byte-identical to v0.5.0.
Raw prompts, model outputs, private host identifiers, and raw request logs are excluded.
